score_100.reason: Figure shows a spike raster and trial-averaged PSTH for an example PMd neuron. The core is to show how choice selectivity, stimulus-difficulty modulation, and single-trial variability jointly support the latent dynamical model. The graph is a two-panel raster-plus-PSTH figure and is worth 35 points. The analysis window from 120 ms after stimulus onset to the reaction time of each trial is a key methodological detail and is worth 20 points. The scientific interpretation is split into two items: systematic modulation of firing rate by choice direction and difficulty is worth 25 points, and the interpretation that single-trial variability reflects differences in latent decision-variable trajectories is worth 20 points. Point allocation: graph reproduction 35, analysis window 20, choice selectivity 25, meaning of single-trial variability 20.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Figure shows the single-trial spike raster and corresponding PSTH for an example PMd neuron during the perceptual decision-making task. The neuron is choice selective: firing rate is higher for right choices than for left choices, easy-stimulus conditions change more rapidly, and hard-stimulus conditions change more slowly. The raster shows that even within the same condition, spike timing and reaction time vary substantially across trials. The core conclusion is that single-trial firing differences reflect random trajectory differences of the latent decision variable x(t) across trials, rather than only Poisson noise.

Scoring items.criterion: Shows a spike raster and trial-averaged firing rate (PSTH) for an example PMd neuron. Raster displays individual trials grouped by condition with reaction times marked. PSTH shows firing rate traces for four conditions (left/right choice and easy/hard difficulty).
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 30 points if misidentified as boxplot, scatter, or model plot. Deduct 15 points if either raster or PSTH is missing. Deduct 10 points if conditions are not distinguishable. Do not deduct for color choice, layout style.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly describes the neuron's choice selectivity and difficulty modulation: firing rate separates by chosen side (higher for right-choice trials), easy-stimulus conditions show faster/steeper rate changes, hard-stimulus conditions show slower/shallower changes. The four condition traces gradually separate after stimulus onset.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 30 points if choice-direction effect is reversed or not described. Deduct 15 points if difficulty modulation is not described. Deduct 10 points if choice selectivity is misinterpreted as stimulus-side selectivity rather than chosen side.

Scoring items.criterion: Notes that even within the same condition, spike timing and reaction time vary across trials in the raster, indicating meaningful trial-to-trial variability in neural dynamics beyond simple noise.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if trial-to-trial variability is not mentioned or is attributed entirely to random noise. Deduct 10 points if only the PSTH average is discussed without acknowledging single-trial variability visible in the raster.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe the raster plot as a single-trial spike raster.
It is acceptable to describe PSTH as trial-averaged firing-rate curves.
It is acceptable to describe black dots as reaction times or reaction-time markers.
It is acceptable to describe higher firing for right choices as this example neuron being right-choice preferring.
Easy/hard stimuli may be described as high/low color coherence or easy/hard trials.
rubric.Scoring instructions: High scores (85-100) require correctly reproducing the raster-plus-PSTH two-panel structure, explaining the analysis window from 120 ms to reaction time, accurately describing choice-direction and difficulty modulation of firing rate, and explaining the relationship between single-trial variability and latent decision-variable trajectories. Partial scores (40-84) should be assigned when the graph structure and choice selectivity are broadly correct but the window definition or single-trial variability interpretation is incomplete. Low scores (0-39) should be assigned when the panel is confused with another graph type, trial-by-trial information in the raster is ignored, chosen side is confused with stimulus side, or single-trial variability is treated entirely as noise.
